# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary task is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must satisfy circle constraints (straight through white, turn at black)
- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be midpoints of straight line segments

### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
*Loop passes through cell centers*

#### 1.2.1 With Directional Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Wind direction restricts loop movement; arrow cells define direction
- **Suraromu** — Loop must pass through all "Gates" in a numbered order

#### 1.2.2 With Regional Constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop must go straight or turn consistently through all circles in each bold-line region
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each room once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms

#### 1.2.3 With Cell-State Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction
- **Masyu** — *(see 1.1)*

---

## 2. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*The task involves connecting elements or tracing paths without forming a closed loop*

### 2.1 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping lines

### 2.2 Network Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges; all islands must form one connected network

### 2.3 Movement / Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home regions along straight paths without crossing
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles straight into gray areas; totals must match area numbers

---

## 3. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*The task is to color or shade cells black according to constraints*

### 3.1 Connectivity-Based Shading
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form a connected wall; white cell islands match given numbers
- **Heyawake** — Shaded cells cannot touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row or column; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total visible white cells in cross directions; black cells cannot touch

### 3.2 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must not be rectangles/squares
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares
- **Usowan** — Shade cells with adjacency counts; exactly one number per bold region is intentionally wrong

### 3.3 Tetromino / Polyomino Shading
- **LITS** — Shade exactly four connected cells (tetromino) per region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; shaded cells must connect globally
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black cells) so each bold region contains exactly two black cells

### 3.4 Gravity / Drop Shading
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per number constraints; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

### 3.5 Tile-Based Shading
- **Tilepaint** — Entire tiles (bold-line regions) are colored or not; diagonal-number clues count black cells in a row/column segment; solution forms a recognizable image
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles must lie on shortest path, triangles must not

### 3.6 Clue-Driven Shading (Radial/Directional)
- **Kurotto** — Circles show the sum of connected black cells extending from them
- **Nurimisaki** — Circle cells are "promontories" with exactly one white neighbor; numbers indicate length of white line from promontory

---

## 4. REGION DIVISION GAMES
*The task is to partition the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

### 4.1 Division into Rectangles
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

### 4.2 Division into Fixed-Size Polyominoes
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate boundary line count around a cell

### 4.3 Division into Variable Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — Divide into blocks where each block's size equals its number; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends pointing toward bends

### 4.4 Division into Paired Color Regions
- **Double Choco** — Each block contains a white and a gray area of identical shape; numbers indicate cell count of one color
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains exactly two same-size shaded blocks; all shaded cells connect globally

---

## 5. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The task is to fill cells with numbers according to logical constraints*

### 5.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box without repetition
- **Hitori** — *(also shading; see 3.1)* — Eliminate duplicates per row/column by shading

### 5.2 Room-Based Number Sets
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1 through N; duplicate values in a row/column must be separated by at least that value's distance
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow-black cells indicate which neighbor holds the maximum value; same numbers in adjacent rooms cannot touch

### 5.3 Block-Size Encoding
- **Fillomino** — *(also region division; see 4.3)* — Numbers encode the size of the block they belong to
- **Chained Block** — Black cell groups are "blocks"; numbers/? label block size; blocks must chain corner-to-corner; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

### 5.4 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill grid with numbers from a given list; numbers read left-to-right or top-to-bottom; one digit per cell

### 5.5 Snake / Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch sides; directional visibility rules restrict placement

---

## 6. OBJECT PLACEMENT GAMES
*The task is to place discrete objects (bulbs, squares, blocks) into the grid*

### 6.1 Light / Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; numbered black cells constrain adjacent bulb count; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

### 6.2 Shape / Block Placement
- **Evolomino** — Place squares in cells forming blocks; each block contains one arrow; blocks along an arrow's path grow by one cell each step without rotation/flipping

### 6.3 Pencil / Line-Object Placement
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil objects (straight cell groups with a tip); draw lines from tips through a number of cells equal to the pencil's number

---

## 7. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining two or more primary mechanics in inseparable ways*

| Game | Primary Mechanics Combined |
|---|---|
| **Dotchi-Loop** | Loop-drawing + regional consistency constraint |
| **Yajilin** | Loop-drawing + cell shading |
| **Nurimeizu** | Cell shading + pathfinding (maze) |
| **Nurimisaki** | Cell shading + connectivity + directional counting |
| **Sto-stone** | Cell shading + gravity simulation |
| **Juosan** | Symbol placement (— or \|) + regional counting + adjacency run-length constraints |

---

## Summary Tree

```
Grid-Based Logic Games
├── 1. Loop-Drawing
│   ├── 1.1 Dot-to-dot loop (Slitherlink, Masyu, Mid-loop)
│   └── 1.2 Cell-traversal loop
│       ├── Directional (Nagareru, Suraromu)
│       └── Regional (Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Yajilin)
├── 2. Path / Connection
│   ├── Pair connection (Numberlink)
│   ├── Network connection (Hashiwokakero)
│   └── Movement / Migration (Satogaeri, Yosenabe)
├── 3. Cell Shading / Painting
│   ├── Connectivity-based (Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko)
│   ├── Shape-constrained (Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Usowan)
│   ├── Tetromino/Polyomino (LITS, Norinori)
│   ├── Gravity/Drop (Sto-stone)
│   ├── Tile-based (Tilepaint, Nurimeizu)
│   └── Clue-driven radial (Kurotto, Nurimisaki)
├── 4. Region Division
│   ├── Into rectangles (Shikaku)
│   ├── Into fixed polyominoes (Five Cells)
│   ├── Into variable polyominoes (Fillomino, Sashigane)
│   └── Into paired color regions (Double Choco, Nuritwin)
├── 5. Number Placement
│   ├── Latin square (Sudoku, Hitori)
│   ├── Room-based sets (Ripple Effect, Makaro)
│   ├── Block-size encoding (Fillomino, Chained Block)
│   ├── Crossword-style (Nansuke)
│   └── Sequential/Snake (Hebi)
├── 6. Object Placement
│   ├── Illumination (Akari)
│   ├── Shape/Block (Evolomino)
│   └── Pencil/Line-object (Pencils)
└── 7. Hybrid / Multi-mechanic
    (Dotchi-Loop, Yajilin, Nurimeizu,
     Nurimisaki, Sto-stone, Juosan)
```
